reason: Reproduced exactly, on both grounds and both publication branches, at 390/768/1440. Direct ?state=publish loads .b-live empty on paper and ink, so every captured frame is clean and the line exists only on the driven path - which is why nine rounds missed it. Driving it: owner-flight -> Publish paints .b-live with "The link is below."; owner-draft -> Publish paints "Ready to send. The link is below." At 390x844 the draft branch measures link field 752..819, the Copy row 848..887, .b-live 899..919 at 13px in solid var(--fore) - the exact numbers the finding gives, byte-identical in ink (rgb(255,255,255)). At 1440x960 it is link 553..581 / Copy 610..649 / live 661..681; at 768x1024 link 765..812 / live 892..912. So the sentence naming a direction sits 80-147px BELOW the thing it points at, on every width, on both grounds, in both branches, and it is the loudest plain sentence in the foot: full ink against the .b-note beneath it at fore-62. The code reading is right too - render-b.js:1805 builds this .b-live with no .b-vh, unlike the owner-shell copies at 1475 and 1536, and go() at 1450 writes SAID.publish (1425) into it. Not already handled: the panel has ruled on this string twice (round 5 publish-says-three-things kept it, round 7 taste--publish-is-not-a-ceremony told the build to drop it and the build conditionalised it instead) but both rulings were about redundancy with the card and the headline; neither looked at where the line lands or noticed it was painted at all. Round 8 ux--new-plan-claims-it-is-already-public called it "the announced strap" while driving past it. Not a restated gate: interaction-check L1369 asserts only that .b-live is non-empty after the press. Not a constraint violation. The one real defence is that this is a role=status line written for the ear, delivered while focus sits on .b-pressTitle - and I verified the first Tab from that title is the link field, so at the moment of delivery "below" is true for the listener. That defence covers the announcement, not the paint. The product paints it, and on a phone it is worse than the finding says: at 390x844 the owner must scroll past the fold to reach Copy at 848, and the line that arrives under their thumb says the link is below while the link is 147px above it. Four words of full-ink copy describing a direction that does not exist, at the foot of the screen that hands the day over, is not terse - it is wrong, and it costs two words to remove. Confirmed on the observation; the finding’s own fix is where it fails and is replaced below.
sharpenedFix: Do NOT split the node as proposed. The suggested h("p.b-liveNav.b-vh") does not carry .b-live, so document.querySelector(".b-live") on the publish screen would return the visible node the fix leaves empty, and interaction-check.mjs L1369-1373 ("publish says where it went", which asserts .b-live is non-empty after the press) flips from passing to failing - the 621/0 gate breaks. Giving the hidden node .b-live instead only moves the damage: the press block’s copy handler (render-b.js:1815) does node.querySelector(".b-live") and would then write "Link copied." into the hidden node, so the visible confirmation the strap was drawn for goes silent on screen and "copy answers out loud" (L1099) passes only by reading the invisible one. The defect does not need a second node. It is one string. In render-b.js:1428-1432 change SAID.publish to return F_PUBLISHED() ? "The link is ready to copy." : "Ready to send." - both name a state rather than a direction, both keep the announcement non-empty so L1369 stays green, neither restates the 15 July date that round 7 ruled the headline already carries, and the copy handler still overwrites the same node with "Link copied." / "Copy did not work. Select the link and copy it by hand.", which is what it was drawn for. Two lines changed, no new node, no gate touched.
